text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh held talks in Hanoi on Saturday with Algerian deputy foreign affairs minister Amar Bendjama to discuss trade, science and economic cooperation programmes.

-- Sweden's SIDA (Swedish International Development Agency) has said it will broaden its 27-year-old assistance programme for Vietnam with help being extended to five mountain provinces in the north of the country.

-- Vietnam sold an estimated 1.9 million tonnes of rice to overseas buyers in the first eight months of this year and is likely to exceed the fixed quota of 2.0 million tonnes thanks to record food output.
-- Nineteen cases involving the trafficking of wild animals have been discovered at the Mong Cai border gate with China in the last four months.
-- Water-levels in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta have reached a very high level. Evacuation has begun in areas facing possible landslides.

-- A British Consultants Bureau delegation led by the Duke of Gloucester began a one-week official visit to Vietnam on September 29. The visit was at the invitation of Vietnam's Minister of Planning and Investment Do Quoc Sam.

-- The Vietnam Apatite Company expects a total output of 600,000 tonnes of apatite ore in 1996. So far this year the company has supplied 425,000 tonnes of apatize ore for fertilizer manufacture, ten percent more than the same period last year.
-- The Hanoi Municipal People's Committee has issued a regulation banning the disposal of garbage on city streets.
-- Professor Vu Tuyen Hoang, head of the Agriculture Ministry's Science and Technology council, has been appointed Vice-Chairman of the American Association of Biography Researching Institutes.
